Thomas Massie, a Republican who will exit Congress next year after losing his primary to a candidate endorsed by President Donald Trump, introduced articles of impeachment against Hegseth. The measures have earned support from nearly all of the Democrats in the House including the likely next speaker, Hakeem Jeffries. Since then, Trump and his senior team have rallied around Hegseth. And it worked. On Tuesday evening the House voted on near party lines 211–204 to refer the bill to the Judiciary Committee, effectively killing it. Eleven Democrats who might have approved of the impeachment appear to have missed or sat out the vote. queue.title: Consumer inflation rises faster than expected in October, CPI report shows
queue.dek: The Labor Department released the latest consumer price index data for October, which showed CPI inflation rose 0.4% on a monthly basis.
queue.opening: Inflation accelerated in October as the pace of consumer price growth trended higher. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said on Wednesday that the consumer price index (CPI) – a broad measure of how much everyday goods like gasoline, groceries and rent cost – increased 0.4% on a monthly basis. It did not release an annual figure due to last year's government shutdown that prevented collection of October 2025 data. The monthly figure was slightly higher than the estimates of economists polled by LSEG, who expected inflation to rise 0.3% from the prior month. So-called core prices, which exclude volatile measurements of gasoline and groceries to better assess price growth trends, were up 0.3% in October. That figure is slightly higher than the 0.2% estimate of economists polled by LSEG. Like with headline CPI, the BLS was unable to release a year-over-year figure for core CPI due to last year's government shutdown disrupting data collection. High inflation has created severe financial pressures in recent years for most U.S. households, which are forced to pay more for everyday necessities like food and rent. Price hikes are particularly difficult for lower-income Americans because they tend to spend more of their already-stretched paychecks on necessities and have less flexibility to save.
